uncertainty_budget.explanation: The Indian market price of the token against the official rupee rate for a dollar. This is the bulk of the gap and it is the part everyone argues about.
No rate was published on the settlement date. Stepping back to 2026-06-25 or forward to 2026-06-29 is undetermined — Rule 206 does not say which.
A daily candle is not a price. It is a range with four printed readings and no rule choosing between them.
The retrieved pair is USDT/INR. The receipt was USDC. The figure is USDT/INR x USDC/USDT, and treating the peg as exactly 1.0000 is a further choice.

regimes.outcome: The receipt of 5,000 USDC is classified as income from the transfer of a virtual digital asset, taxed at 30% under s.115BBH. The valuation date is the date of receipt (2026-06-28). The fair market value is determined using the telegraphic transfer buying rate of USDC on the last day of the tax year (2026-03-31). No TDS obligation arises as the recipient is outside India. Under s.439(8), a bona fide explanation and disclosure of all material facts are required to avoid penalties.
regimes.reasoning: The receipt of 5,000 USDC is classified as income from the transfer of a virtual digital asset under s.115BBH, which taxes such transfers at 30%. The valuation date is determined by Rule 56, which specifies the date of receipt (2026-06-28). The fair market value is determined using the telegraphic transfer buying rate of USDC on the last day of the tax year (2026-03-31) as per Rule 206. No TDS obligation arises because the recipient is outside India, as per the TDS rules in s.393(1). Under s.439(8), a bona fide explanation and disclosure of all material facts are required to avoid penalties.
